messages.content:
You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Yours sincerely,  

Authorized Signatory  
Claims Department, Jeevan Setu General Insurance

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for

- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.

- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.

- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

messages.content:
You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter

"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date

- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

- admission_date

messages.content:
You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Yours faithfully,

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.

- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

We have examined the claim submitted for the amount of Rs 5,17,000 in respect of the treatment for end‑stage renal disease requiring dialysis received at Shanti Multispeciality Hospital, Pune. After a detailed review of the medical records provided by the hospital, it has been observed that the records indicate a history of chronic kidney disease extending for seven (7) years prior to the commencement of your policy.

If you wish to discuss this decision, please contact our Grievance Redressal Officer at grievance@nirbhayhealth.com or call 1800‑123‑4567 within 30 days of receipt of this letter.

Yours sincerely,

Subject: Rejection of Claim – Hospitalisation for Coronary Angiography  

Dear Ms. Das,  

Without prejudice, we refer to your claim dated 25.09.2022 for the amount of INR 45,000 submitted in respect of treatment received at Sai Krupa Nursing Home, Nashik, wherein you were admitted at 08:00 hrs on 02.08.2022 and discharged at 15:00 hrs on 02.08.2022 for coronary angiography. After a thorough review of the documentation and in accordance with Clause 5.2 (Medical Necessity) and Clause 9.1 (Hospitalisation Eligibility) of the policy wording, we hereby inform you that the claim is rejected on the ground that the hospitalisation was not medically necessary because the same procedure could have been performed on an outpatient (OPD) basis.  

The policy expressly provides that hospitalisation benefits are payable only where admission is required for an illness or injury that cannot be treated on an outpatient basis and where the duration of stay exceeds the minimal observation period for a day‑care procedure (Clause 10.4). Coronary angiography is listed in the Day‑Care Procedures Schedule and is therefore covered only when performed as a stay of less than twenty‑four (24) hours; the admission recorded exceeds that threshold, rendering the claim non‑eligible.  

Consequently, the amount claimed of INR 45,000 is denied and no further payment will be made. Should you wish to appeal this decision, you may submit a written request within thirty (30) days from the date of this letter, specifying any additional documentation in accordance with Clause 13.2 (Appeals Procedure). This correspondence does not prejudice any rights of the insurer under the policy.  

Yours faithfully,  

[Name]

- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement

- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date

- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for

- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Aarogya Kavach Health Insurance
Letter Date: 06/09/2020

Mr. Devendra Nair
Policy No: AK/FLT/2019/977739
Claim No: CLM-2020-4760612

Dear Mr. Nair,

Thank you for contacting us and for your continued trust in Aarogya Kavach Health Insurance. We sincerely apologise for any inconvenience you may have experienced during the claim process and we appreciate the patience you have shown.

We have carefully reviewed your claim for the hospitalization at Shanti Multispeciality Hospital, Pune, with the date of admission on 08/07/2020. The treatment recorded was coronary angiography and the amount claimed is ₹4,10,000. Our records indicate that the patient was in hospital for 10 hours.

After a thorough assessment of the medical information provided, we regret to inform you that the hospitalization was not medically necessary, as the coronary angiography could have been performed on an outpatient (OPD) basis. We apologise for any disappointment this decision may cause.

Consequently, we are unable to honour the claim in full. The payable amount under this claim is ₹0.00. We understand that this may be disappointing and we apologise again for any inconvenience caused.

If you have any further queries or require additional clarification, please do not hesitate to contact our Customer Care Team. We remain committed to serving you and appreciate the opportunity to address your concerns.

Yours sincerely,

Customer Care Officer
Aarogya Kavach Health Insurance
Grievance Cell: grievance@aarogyakavach.com

REJECTION LETTER:
Aarogya Kavach Health Insurance  
Via MediSetu TPA Services  
123 Health Avenue, Mumbai, Maharashtra  

Letter Date: October 23, 2023  

To,  
Ms. Meenakshi Chauhan  

Subject: Claim Settlement Advice – Claim No. CLM-2023-7788515  

Dear Ms. Chauhan,

We refer to your claim submitted for hospitalization at Navjeevan Hospital, Ahmedabad, admission date October 4, 2023, for dengue fever, under policy number AK/HLT/2022/128184.

After verification, we note that the policy was not in force on the date of admission as the renewal premium for the policy period ending July 24, 2023 was due on July 25, 2023 and was received only on August 7, 2023, i.e., after the expiry of the grace period. Consequently, the claim is not payable.

The details of the amount considered are shown below:

+-----------------+------------+  
| Description     | Amount     |  
+-----------------+------------+  
| Claimed Amount  | Rs 3,82,000|  
| Approved Amount | Rs 0       |  
+-----------------+------------+  

Remarks:  
- The policy lapsed on July 25, 2023 due to non‑receipt of renewal premium within the stipulated period.  
- Renewal premium was received on August 7, 2023, which is after the policy lapse date.  
- As the policy was not in effect on the date of admission, no benefits are payable under this claim.  

If you wish to discuss this decision, please contact our Claims Helpline at 1800-555-1234 within 30 days of this letter.

Sincerely,  

Authorized Signatory  
Claims Department  
Aarogya Kavach Health Insurance  

Grievance Redressal: grievance@aarogyakavach.com

Samriddhi Health Insurance
Corporate Office, 12th Floor, Business Plaza,
Bandra West, Mumbai – 40005O

Date: 16-Jan-2024

Ms. Shabnam D'Souza
[Residential Address]

Subject: Short‑settlement of Claim No. CLM-2023-8973750 under Po1icy No. SH/IND/2020/842253

Dear Ms. D'Souza,

We refer to your claim dated 02-Dec-2023 for treatment received at Sai Krupa Nursing Home Nashik, wherein a laparoscopic cholecystectomy was performed and a tota1 bill of Rs 1,53,000 was submitted. After a detailed examination of the documents furnished and in accordance with the provisions of the Policy Wording, specifically Clause 5.2 (Room Rent Entitlement) and Clause 7.1 (Settlement of Claims) we hereby issue this short‑settlement communication.

Without prejudice to any rights or remedies available to Samriddhi Health Insurance under the policy, we have determined that the room category occupied by the insured was charged at Rs 5,000 per day for a period of 8 days, which exceeds the entitlement stipulated in the policy. Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Subject: Decision on Claim CLM-2024-1893537

22-Feb-2024

Dear Ms. Geeta Iyer,

Thank you for submitting your claim under Policy No. DG/HLT/2022/161391 for the amount of ₹4,26,000. The claim pertains to treatment received at Navjeevan Hospital, Ahmedabad, with admission on 13-Jan-2024 for spinal disc surgery following a road traffic accident.

We have carefully reviewed the details of your claim. Under the terms of your policy, intervertebral disc prolapse is classified as a specific disease and is subject to a waiting period of 24 months. The policy provides that only the initial 30‑day waiting period is waived when treatment follows an accident; the specific disease waiting period is not waived in such circumstances. You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.

- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.

- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".
