Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement

- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date

- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent

- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

Subject: Rejection of Claim – Policy No. SH/IND/2020/768824 – Claim No. CLM-2020-1678056 – Without prejudice  

Dear Ms. Gill,  

We refer to your claim dated 22 October 2020 in respect of hospitalization at Sai Krupa Nursing Home, Nashik, for the treatment of a head injury sustained in a two‑wheeler accident on 19 October 2020, for which an amount of Rs 5,57,000 was claimed.  

Pursuant to Clause 5.2 of the Policy Wordings and the provisions set out in the Schedule of Benefits, the Policy issued to you on 11 October 2020 is subject to an initial waiting period of thirty (30) days from the date of inception, a condition expressly applicable to all claims arising from any illness or injury unless specifically excluded by the clause relating to accidents. While the waiting period clause does provide an exception for claims arising out of an accident, the referenced provision (Clause 5.3) clarifies that the initial waiting period remains applicable to any claim where the treatment is for a condition that is not categorically covered as an accident‑related injury under the definition stipulated in Clause 4.1.  

Given that the head injury, although resulting from a vehicular accident, is classified under the category of “injury requiring medical attention” and does not fall within the narrow definition of “accident‑related injury” as contemplated by Clause 4.1, the claim therefore falls within the scope of the initial thirty (30) day waiting period. Consequently, the claim is not payable under the terms of the Policy.  

Accordingly, we hereby reject the claim for Rs 5,57,000. This decision is made without prejudice to any rights that Samriddhi Health Insurance may have under the Policy or applicable law, and is final in respect of the present claim. Should you wish to discuss this decision further, you may contact our Grievance Redressal Officer at grievance@samriddhihealth.in or call 1800‑450‑1234 between 9:00 am and 6:00 pm on weekdays.  

Yours faithfully,  

_________________________

- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date

- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not

- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter

- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period

- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement

- admission_date

- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.

We refer to your claim dated December 24, 2024, for treatment rendered at Lotus Care Hospital, Hyderabad, for an acute myocardial infarction with angioplasty, for which an amount of INR 1,43,000 was claimed under the above‑referenced policy.  

Without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to Suraksha General Insurance under the policy contract, we hereby inform you that the claim is denied in accordance with Clause 5.2 (Pre‑existing Disease Waiting Period) and Section 3(b) (Exclusions) of the policy wordings, the relevant provisions of which expressly stipulate that any claim arising from a disease declared as pre‑existing and for which the waiting period of forty‑eight (48) months has not been completed shall be excluded from cover.  

As per the declaration made in the proposal form, coronary artery disease was identified as a pre‑existing condition. Accordingly, the period of continuous cover since the date of first inception, i.e., January 6, 2021, does not satisfy the prescribed pre‑existing disease waiting period of four (4) years for coronary artery disease, and therefore the claim falls within the exclusionary clause.  

Consequently, the amount claimed of INR 1,43,000 is not payable under the terms of the policy. Should you wish to seek clarification regarding this decision, you may direct your correspondence to our Grievance Redressal Officer at grievance@swasthyamitratpa.com within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter, in accordance with the grievance handling procedure prescribed under Clause 9.1 of the policy.  

Yours faithfully,  

_________________________  
Senior Claims Officer  
Suraksha General Insurance

messages.content:
You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Subject: Rejection of Claim – Hospitalisation Benefit  

Without prejudice, and pursuant to the terms and conditions of the above‑referenced policy, in particular Clause 5.2 (Hospitalisation Benefit) and Clause 7.1 (Medical Necessity), we hereby inform you that your claim for the amount of ₹2,79,000 relating to the admission at Aastha Hospital, Jaipur on 14/08/2025 for observation and IV fluids for acute gastritis is rejected.  

The policy expressly provides that hospitalisation benefit is payable only when admission is medically necessary and cannot be managed on an outpatient (OPD) basis. Consequently, the claim does not satisfy the conditions precedent for the hospitalisation benefit and is hereby denied.  

Please note that this decision is final under the policy terms, and any further correspondence should be addressed to the Grievance Redressal Officer at grievance@surakshainsurance.in.  

Yours faithfully,  

[Signature]  
Claims Officer  
Suraksha General Insurance

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.

- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

- admission_date

messages.content:
You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

Jeevan Setu General Insurance  
Through its TPA – Swasthya Mitra TPA  

Date: 26 October 2024  

To,  
Harpreet Kulkarni  

Subject: Claim No. CLM-2024-7896970 – Rejection of Claim  

1. We refer to your claim under Policy No. JS/HLT/2022/576402 for the hospitalization at Shanti Multispeciality Hospital, Pune, dated 28 September 2024, for the diagnosis of inguinal hernia and the amount claimed of Rs 5,04,000.  

2. We regret to inform you that after a detailed verification, the claim falls within the specific disease waiting period of twenty‑four (24) months applicable to inguinal hernia. As the admission occurred within this waiting period, the claim is not admissible for settlement. Kindly note that the policy terms expressly provide for this waiting period for specified diseases.  

3. The same shall be recorded in your claim file. Should you wish to seek clarification or appeal the decision, you may contact our Grievance Redressal Cell at grievance@jeevansetuins.com or call 1800‑123‑4567 within thirty (30) days from the date of this letter.  

Thank you for your understanding.  

Yours faithfully,  

_____________________  
Chief Claims Officer  
Jeevan Setu General Insurance

Current Policy Period: 24 December 2023 to 23 December 2024  

Waiting Periods:  
- Initial waiting period: 30 days from the date of policy commencement.

The policy provides coverage as per the terms and conditions outlined in the master policy document, subject to the above waiting periods and other standard exclusions.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.

- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any

- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

Without prejudice to any rights or remedies available to Nirbhay Health Assurance under the policy issued to you and in accordance with the provisions of Clause 4.1(a) of the policy wording, we hereby inform you that your claim for the sum of ₹1,26,000, arising from the hospitalization at Lotus Care Hospital, Hyderabad, on 27.07.2026 for the treatment of status epilepticus, is rejected in totality on the basis of non‑disclosure of a pre‑existing disease as defined in Clause 5.2(b) of the policy.

In view of the foregoing, and as per the provisions governing pre‑existing conditions, the claim is hereby denied. Should you wish to appeal this decision, you may do so in writing within thirty (30) days from the date of this letter, referring to the above claim number and quoting the relevant policy clauses.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)

- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date

- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter

- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used

- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".

You review rejected Indian health insurance claims. You are given a rejection (or short-settlement) letter and an excerpt of the policy. Decide whether the rejection is worth contesting. Do not give false hope: say likely_contestable only when the documents support it.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"category", "facts", "verdict", "reason", "ask_insurer_for"

category: the insurer's ground, one of
- non_disclosure_ped: a pre-existing disease was allegedly not declared in the proposal form
- waiting_period: the claim falls inside an initial, specific-disease or pre-existing-disease waiting period
- permanent_exclusion: the treatment is said to be permanently excluded
- no_hospitalisation_needed: hospitalisation was said to be unnecessary (could be OPD)
- room_rent_proportionate: a proportionate deduction for a room above entitlement
- documents_or_late_intimation: missing documents, late intimation or late submission
- policy_lapsed: the policy was said to be not in force (renewal premium)
- sum_insured_exhausted: the sum insured was said to be used up
- other: anything else

facts: an object with ALL of these keys. Use null when the documents do not state or show it. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD.
- policy_inception_date: start of continuous cover, including cover ported from an earlier insurer (not the current policy period)
- admission_date
- months_continuous_coverage: whole completed months from policy_inception_date to admission_date
- condition_named_by_insurer: the disease the insurer names, if any
- ped_disclosed_in_proposal: true if the policy shows the named disease was declared, false if it shows it was not
- condition_related_to_claim: is the named disease medically related to the illness claimed for
- waiting_period_months: the waiting period the insurer relies on, in months (30 days = 1)
- is_accident: true if the claim arose from an accident, false if from illness
- accident_exempt_in_wording: true if the policy says accidents are exempt from that waiting period, false if it says they are not
- exclusion_cited: the exclusion the insurer cites, if any
- exclusion_in_policy_wording: true if that exclusion appears in the policy excerpt, false if a list of exclusions is given and it is absent
- hospital_stay_hours: hours from admission to discharge
- is_listed_daycare_procedure: true if the treatment is in the policy's day care list, false if a list is given and it is absent
- room_rent_limit_per_day: INR, from the policy
- room_rent_charged_per_day: INR, from the letter
- premium_paid_within_grace: true if the renewal premium was received within the grace period after the due date
- restore_benefit_available_unused: true if the policy has a restore benefit not yet used this policy year, false if there is none or it was used
- crc_approval_mentioned: true if the letter says the Claims Review Committee approved the decision, otherwise false

verdict: likely_contestable, worth_asking or likely_valid. First check the grounds that make a rejection contestable. If any is clearly met, answer likely_contestable. If none is met but one cannot be checked because a fact is null, answer worth_asking. Otherwise use the fallback.
- non_disclosure_ped: contestable if months_continuous_coverage >= 60 (moratorium), or the disease was in fact disclosed. Otherwise worth_asking if the disease is unrelated to the claim; else likely_valid.
- waiting_period: contestable if it is an accident and the waiting period is 1 month or less; or it is an accident, the waiting period is longer and the policy exempts accidents; or months_continuous_coverage >= waiting_period_months. Otherwise likely_valid.
- permanent_exclusion: contestable if the cited exclusion is not in the policy wording. Otherwise likely_valid.
- no_hospitalisation_needed: contestable if the stay was 24 hours or more, or the treatment is a listed day care procedure. Otherwise worth_asking.
- room_rent_proportionate: contestable if the room rent charged is not above the limit. Otherwise worth_asking.
- documents_or_late_intimation: always worth_asking.
- policy_lapsed: contestable if the premium was paid within the grace period. Otherwise likely_valid.
- sum_insured_exhausted: worth_asking if an unused restore benefit is available; null means worth_asking; otherwise likely_valid.
- other: always worth_asking.

reason: plain English, at most 80 words, for a family member, naming the facts that decide it.
ask_insurer_for: up to 6 short items. Always start with "The exact policy clause relied on". Unless the letter mentions Claims Review Committee approval, add "Confirmation that the Claims Review Committee approved this repudiation".
